newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC acts to preserve diesel competition.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC acts to preserve diesel competition.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission said it reached an agreement with the German firm Mahle GmbH to preserve competition in the diesel engine pistons market.

It said the accord is to prevent Mahle from exercising any control over competitor Metal Leve SA Industria a Comercio of Brazil, in which Mahle acquired a controlling interest last June without U.S. antitrust review.
Both firms make diesel engine parts, including pistons, through U.S. units -- Mahle Inc., in Morristown, Tenn., and Metal Leve Inc, in Ann Arbor, Michigan.
The FTC said the "hold separate" agreement prevents immediate anticompetitive effects and preserves its ability to prevent higher prices or other anticompetitive effects.
It also enables the agency to maintain competition should its investigation of the acquisition find that it violated U.S. antitrust law.
